summary: Ni/A1203 catalysts were prepared by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) using vaporized Ni(acac)2 and air. The nickel content was controlled by repeating reaction cycles, and the preheat temperature of alumina influenced catalyst activity. The highest activity was observed for catalysts with 10 wt% nickel prepared from alumina preheated at 875~.
evidence: Ni/A1203 catalysts were prepared by saturating gas-solid reactions as an atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) process. Vaporized Ni(acac)2 was chemisorbed on a porous alumina support, and the produced surface complex was then air treated to remove the ligand residues. The nickel content could be precisely controlled by repeating this reactor cycle. The preheat temperature of alumina influenced the activity of the catalyst, and a maximum in the activity was observed for catalysts prepared from alumina preheated at 875~.
